text_blocks.snippet: In 2021, the United States experienced a significant surge in inflation, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising by 7.0% from December 2020 to December 2021, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics (.gov). This was the largest year-over-year increase since 1981. Food prices also rose considerably, increasing by 6.3% over the year.
snippet_highlighted_words: the United States experienced a significant surge in inflation, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising by 7.0% from December 2020 to December 2021

text_blocks.snippet: Several factors contributed to the inflationary environment in 2021, including:

list.title: Supply chain disruptions:
list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic caused significant disruptions to global supply chains, leading to shortages of various goods and driving up prices.

list.title: Increased demand:
list.snippet: As economies reopened after pandemic lockdowns, pent-up demand led to increased spending, putting pressure on prices.

list.title: Monetary and fiscal policies:
list.snippet: Government stimulus measures and accommodative monetary policy contributed to increased liquidity in the economy, further fueling demand.
